$comment: The status machine (H23), written once and asserted on both sides of the wire.
The server decides status in backend/app/services/item_status.py. The iPad predicts it
optimistically in frontend/lib/consumption.ts so a Consume tap feels instant, which means
the rule is written twice and can drift - and while it is drifting the card shows a label
the server will contradict a round trip later.
So both read this file: backend/tests/crud/test_quantity_status.py and
frontend/lib/__tests__/consumption.test.ts. A change to either implementation that is not
a change to this file fails one of the two suites.
'opened' is whether the pack has ever been opened (opened_date is set). It decides the
full-again case: a sealed pack corrected upward is still sealed, anything else reads
opened, because a jar does not re-seal itself.
Cases whose event is not 'consume' are backend-only - the client never predicts a
correction, a discard or a restore - and are marked serverOnly.

cases.name: exactly three quarters left still reads opened
an opened pack eaten down past the threshold
correcting an empty item back up refills it, but it was opened
correcting an empty item part way up
correcting a partial item above full no longer keeps the stale label
correcting a sealed item above full leaves it sealed
a mis-tap put it in the bin; it comes back opened, never sealed
restoring something that was already finished

refused.name: a thrown-away item cannot be eaten
a thrown-away item cannot be corrected
